Between project initiation on June 1, 2022, and termination on October 9, 2025, the UDERMS team completed foundational design, modeling, and integration work across all major technical tasks for all of Budget Period 1 and most of Budget Period 2. Achievements include grid modelling for all participating customer locations, the configuration and testing of a Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) solution that was integrated with an new Energy Management System (EMS) instance in a sandbox environment, deployment of multiple Open Automated Demand Response (OpenADR) virtual top nodes (VTN) and virtual end nodes (VEN), installation of advanced meter infrastructure (AMI) meters, connected to ~170 electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) infrastructure at multiple pilot sites, detailed development and implementation of cybersecurity and business model frameworks, demand response technology evaluation for water heater and HVAC retrofits, energy efficiency (EE) modelling for all buildings, initial validation of hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulations demonstrating distributed energy resource (DER) based grid services, and field testing of DER controls at the microgrid facility. The project successfully defined the control architecture, communication pathways, and grid service parameters for frequency support, peak load management, and contingency reserves, while advancing EE modeling for six participating facilities showing energy savings exceeding 30% relative to baseline. Key documents finalized prior to termination include the DER initial control configuration, the inventory of all DERs and AMI installations, the plan for business model development, Cybersecurity Plan (Phase B), Intellectual Property Plan, preliminary Evaluation and Measurement (M&V) Plan, and all EE modeling reports. Although the project was terminated prior to full field deployment and long-term demonstration, the work completed established replicable frameworks for integrating DERs into utility operations and national connected community initiatives. The technical progress and lessons learned from UDERMS provide valuable contributions to ongoing industry and DOE efforts aimed at advancing secure, efficient, and scalable community energy solutions. 4 5 Project Summary The UDERMS iCommunity project planned to implement a utility managed “behind the meter” DER control program to integrate diverse types of buildings with a range of flexible loads to optimize grid services and improve building energy efficiency. The optimized grid services included demand response such as peak load management, frequency support, and contingency reserves.
